items.title: Commission sets up new EU Sanctions Office and appoints new EU Sanctions Envoy
items.summary: European Commission Press release Brussels, 18 Nov 2026 Today, the Commission has created the EU Sanctions Office to bring together the Commission's expertise on the entire sanctions lifecycle, from policy design to implementation, enforcement, and anti-circumvention, including outreach to and engagement with third countries.

items.title: Outage Chaos: When Tech is too Big to Fail
items.summary: Outages happen, but we deserve a resilient internet where no one outage at one company can put people at risk and disrupt the global economy. We can only get there by addressing an over-reliance on a few cloud monopolists through effective antitrust laws and interoperability requirements. Service outages, like we’ve seen recently at Microsoft , Apple *, banks , courts , airlines , and elsewhere, can be more than an annoying hurdle. Losing a vital service due to an error can cause the same impacts as a government-ordered internet shutdown—people losing access to vital information and lines of communication. As usual, the greatest harms are faced by people on the margins globally. There’s not much hope in companies out-nerding these issues either. Technical errors will always exist, whether it’s a bug , negligence from an administrator, or a malicious attack. The problem is an over-reliance on any one company or system when these inevitable outages occur. It’s a matter of public safety and economic stability that policymakers mitigate the impact of these disruptions before they occur. items.title: Surveillance Isn't Safety: A Comic About Organizing Against Flock and Other Foes
items.summary: In the new comic "Surveillance Isn't Safety"—available for free today— cartoonist Bryn Adams explores the growing movement against mass surveillance through their involvement in the community fight against Flock Safety in Cleveland, Ohio. It's a personal journey that will resonate widely with residents in hundreds of cities where communities are drawing the line against automated license plate readers (ALPRs). Jump to the Comic Or download the PDF Published in collaboration between EFF and Crucial Comix , Bryn's comic captures the authenticity of the grassroot backlash against the surveillance industry—undercutting Flock founder Garrett Langley's latest dubious defense that public opposition of his company's product isn't real. At the International Association of Chiefs of Police conference this fall, Langley accused the anti-surveillance activism of being driven by Russian bots and as being "inorganic."
